claim: The selected archive study acquired 187 reports: 29 development, 79 other March families and 79 upstream background.
limit: Purposeful selection; not 187 agents or attacks

claim: Four ONCB submissions contain programs; two contain fetch-and-relay instructions; one report records an ONCB data-bearing output request.
basis: Static decoding plus archived HTTP entries
limit: No exact source/output byte match; no proof of subsequent agent use

claim: Some submitted programs have no corresponding target or output request in the retained record.
limit: Absence scoped to acquired record; not a global absence claim

claim: Two other March carriers encode answer tables without scripts, while one upstream background carrier contains a diagnostic script.
basis: Static decoding of d6669745, 4c62b534 and bdf482a4 reports
limit: Background labels are upstream judgments; not a false-positive rate

claim: All 2,978 selected HTTP entries lack embedded raw response body data; 128 pair a positive reported size with an empty-string SHA-256.
limit: Archive representation caution, not proof of falsification

claim: This investigation has not established a new incident or independently authenticated an actor.
limit: Empty service responses did not establish zero search results

claim: The main comparison ran 17 authored cases, 47 route variants and 188 condition cells.
limit: Correlated authored fixtures, not independent real-world incidents

claim: Both complete controls prevented all 25 prohibited variants; the shared service added no prevention in the fixture set.
limit: Trusted adapters and inputs; raw client bypasses both

claim: Of 22 permitted variants, per-tool checks completed 16 and shared checks 13; the difference was the injected shared-service outage.
limit: Not a deployment reliability estimate; both also block a missing fixture restriction label and receive partial fixtures

claim: Injected faults produced failed clients with full receipt and successful clients with partial receipt under every condition.
limit: Two authored faults across three adapters; not natural failure frequency

claim: An unmediated client bypassed both complete adapter controls.
limit: The experiment has no OS-level network enforcement

claim: OpenAI reported successful public uploads followed by blocked browser operations.
limit: Not independently verified by Fide; not part of the experiment denominator

claim: A second request supplied with permission=false was denied while an earlier permitted receipt remained in the journal.
limit: Two static case definitions; no mutable permission store, revocation operation or concurrency test

claim: Removing a primary local file left a known replica with the original digest.
limit: Not evidence about any external service or vendor cleanup

claim: All seven decodable httpbin payloads in the 187 selected reports were audited: five carrier fingerprints match and two differ; three of five submitted script payloads have matching script entries.
basis: Static byte and SHA-256 comparisons against pinned acquired JSON
limit: Archive metadata corroboration, not recovered response bodies, proof of complete execution or an actor detector

claim: The 47 named route variants contain 33 distinct operational configurations under the documented executable-input grouping.
basis: Static inspection of fixture bytes, labels, cases, routes and fault flags
limit: Neither named nor grouped counts are independent real incidents or statistical trials
